verdict_basis: Two demonstrated errors, each with file/line evidence, defeat named spec triggers rather than merely being unimplemented: (F1) Pi writes its own default title AFTER every `session_start` handler returns, at both startup and restoration, so the spec's 'refresh the title on session start, restoration' is deterministically clobbered by the obvious implementation; (F3) the Radar mapping the spec says to reuse matches its regexes against the whole terminal title, which already contains the session name and cwd basename, so a project or session name containing a family word yields a model logo not derived from the selected model — a guessed logo, which bullet 4 forbids. Absence of the extension itself is NOT counted as a defect.

findings.claim: Pi writes its own default terminal title AFTER every `session_start` handler has returned, at both startup and restoration, so a title set from a `session_start` handler is deterministically overwritten. Bullet 2 names session start and restoration as refresh points and acceptance 5a/5b require tests for them; as specified, the straightforward implementation cannot satisfy either.
findings.evidence: pi/dist/core/agent-session.js:2614 `await this._extensionRunner.emit(this._sessionStartEvent)` (inside `bindExtensions`, :2594-2617). pi/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:1584-1603 `rebindCurrentSession`: :1593 `await this.bindCurrentSessionExtensions()` then :1602 `this.updateTerminalTitle()`. Startup entry: interactive-mode.js:783. Resume entry: pi/dist/core/agent-session-runtime.js:128-146 (:111 `beforeSessionInvalidate()` → interactive-mode.js:364 `resetExtensionUI()` → :1914 `updateTerminalTitle()`; :141 session_start reason "resume"; :144 → :120-123 `rebindSession` → interactive-mode.js:367 → :1602). Title writer: interactive-mode.js:810-819. Contrast `session_info_changed`, where pi/dist/core/agent-session.js:3176-3178 emits to the host first (`_emit`, consumed at interactive-mode.js:2800-2801) and to extensions second and unawaited (`void ... .emit(event)`), so an extension handler there does win — i.e. the clobbering is specific to the two refresh points the spec names.

findings.claim: `ModelSelectSource` declares a `"restore"` source, but no code path in the installed build emits it — only `"set"` and `"cycle"`. `model_select` therefore cannot be used as the restoration trigger, and a test or live check written against a restore-sourced model event would never fire.
findings.evidence: pi/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:848 `export type ModelSelectSource = "set" | "cycle" | "restore";`. The only emit sites are pi/dist/core/agent-session.js:1958 (`"set"`), :2012 (`"cycle"`), :2036 (`"cycle"`), all via `_emitModelSelect` (:1926-1935). A content search for `"restore"` across every `pi/dist/**/*.js` returns no matches, and a search for `_emitModelSelect|emitModelSelect` returns only those four lines.

findings.claim: Radar's `modelFor` matches its family regexes against the whole terminal title, and Pi's title already contains the session name and the cwd basename. A project or session whose name contains a family word therefore produces a model logo that was not derived from the selected model — a guessed logo, which bullet 4 forbids. The spec's reuse instruction inherits this behaviour unchanged.
findings.evidence: source/lib/logos.js:259-262 `for (const [family, re] of MODEL_FAMILIES) if (re.test(title ?? '')) return family;` against `MODEL_FAMILIES` at :247-256, including `/\b(claude|opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)\b/i`, `/\b(gpt|o[1-9](-\w+)?|codex)\b/i`, `/\bgrok\b/i`, `/\bqwen\b/i`. Title composition: pi/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:811-818 interpolates `path.basename(this.sessionManager.getCwd())` and `this.sessionManager.getSessionName()`. Radar passes the title through unmodified on this path: source/lib/state.js:300-308 (`vendorTitle`/`stripVendorPulse` only; `locationOnly` at :232-238 keeps any title with a real tail) and source/lib/state.js:475 `modelFor(entry.title, entry.name)` — `trimGroupPrefix` (state.js:429-435) is not applied before the match. Concrete instance: this review's own directory basename, `pi-model-logo-opus-review-recovery`, matches the claude family on `opus`.

findings.claim: Three of the eight model families have no brand hue, so their model marks render in plain ink while the other five render in brand colour. A live check phrased as "the correct logo" (acceptance 5f) can read a correct-but-uncoloured mark as wrong, particularly for a GPT-family selection next to a coral Claude mark.
findings.evidence: source/lib/palette.js:78-88 `brand` covers claude, gemini, kimi, deepseek, qwen, kiro, cline, kilo plus `other`; `gpt`, `grok` and `glm` are absent, while all three are `MODEL_FAMILIES` keys (source/lib/logos.js:248,253,254). findings.claim: If the Pi extension reuses the mapping by importing `source/lib/logos.js` (one of the two readings in U1), first glyph resolution under the default `auto` variant runs a synchronous `spawnSync('fc-match')` with a 3000 ms timeout on Pi's event loop, and the module is CommonJS inside an ESM package.

The result is cached after the first call (logos.js:166-171), so the cost is paid once per process.

findings.claim: Pi tracks no title ownership: `ui.setTitle` is an unrecorded passthrough to the terminal and `resetExtensionUI()` unconditionally reclaims the title to Pi's default. Two extensions setting the title are last-writer-wins with no restore, and the model title is silently dropped on `/reload` until the extension re-applies it.
findings.evidence: pi/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:2068 `setTitle: (title) => this.ui.terminal.setTitle(title)` — no stored value, no key, no per-extension slot (contrast `setStatus(key, text)` at :2055 and `setWidget(key, ...)` at :2065, which are keyed and are cleared per-extension at :1907-1908). interactive-mode.js:1893-1914 `resetExtensionUI()` → :1914 `updateTerminalTitle()`, invoked from :364 and :5345. pi/dist/core/extensions/runner.js:146 the no-op default confirms there is no fallback bookkeeping.

findings.claim: On win32 Pi restores its own title asynchronously after the startup package-update check completes, with no event an extension can hook to re-apply. Whether either target host is affected is not establishable here.
findings.evidence: pi/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:841-853 — the `checkForPackageUpdates()` `.finally()` block: "On Windows, npm can overwrite the shared console title ... Restore Pi's title after the startup check", `if (process.platform === "win32" && this.isInitialized) { this.updateTerminalTitle(); }`. No host OS evidence is available for Darkseid or Alghul in either snapshot.

unknowns.text: Which direction "reuse Radar's existing model-to-logo mapping" means. Reading (a): the Pi extension imports `lib/logos.js` and writes the resolved glyph into its own title. Reading (b): the Pi extension writes only the model name/id, and Radar's existing title-derived mapping (source/lib/state.js:475) produces the glyph, so no new mapping code exists anywhere. The two differ in deliverable, in coupling (F6 applies only to (a)), in where the unknown-model test lives (F4), and in whether the glyph would appear twice (once in Pi's title, once in Radar's `$model` cell). The spec text does not decide it; reading (b) is the cheaper one and is consistent with how the mark is documented to work (source/README.md:95-98, source/CHANGELOG.md:15).

The literal value of `APP_TITLE`, which the extension must reproduce to preserve Pi's title shape, is not in the snapshot: pi/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:14 imports it from `../../config.js`, and no file exists at pi/dist/config.js (only pi/dist/core/**, pi/dist/modes/** and pi/examples/** were supplied).

The spec does not fix where the model token sits in the title. Position determines whether Radar's own title handling interferes: `locationOnly` (source/lib/state.js:232-238) and `trimGroupPrefix` (:429-435, matching a group label plus one of `· ・ ‧ | » : - — –`) both key off the head of the title, and F3's false-positive surface depends on what else shares the string.

Whether Radar's managed sidebar block is installed on either host, and at which glyph variant. The model mark only draws when that block is present (source/lib/managed-config.js:455, installed at :578-614 / :629-643), and the block's rules match literal glyph strings tagged at :376-380 and :532, so a variant mismatch yields a blank cell. No host state was supplied.

Whether Herdr's agent detection reports `pi` for the panes in question — required for `$logo` to be Pi's own mark, which the acceptance phrase "beside Pi's logo" presupposes. Detection is Herdr-side (source/lib/state.js:276-288, `display_agent` override via `pane.report_metadata --display-agent`) and not verifiable offline.

Which discovery location the deployment targets — project-local `cwd/.pi/extensions/` or global `<agentDir>/extensions/` (pi/dist/core/extensions/loader.js:677-682). This changes the rollback blast radius and whether the title changes for every Pi session on the host or only inside one project.

No Pi-side artefact exists in the snapshot to review: the source tree contains only lib/*.js, test/*.test.js, package.json, README.md and CHANGELOG.md — no extension directory, and the referenced bin/ and tools/ scripts (bin/install-font.js at logos.js:172, bin/configure.js at managed-config.js:8, tools/check.js at state.js:931, agent-icons.js at state.js:747) are absent. The spec's work is entirely prospective; per instruction this is recorded as scope, not as a defect.

taste.text: The spec's three triggers do not map one-to-one onto Pi's events: "session start" and "restoration" are the same hook (`session_start`, with `reason` discriminating startup/reload/new/resume/fork — pi/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:554-561), while `session_info_changed` (types.d.ts:1155) is a fourth refresh point the spec omits even though renaming a session rewrites the title (interactive-mode.js:2800-2801) and would drop the model mark. Wording the bullet as "on every Pi title write" would describe the actual surface more honestly than enumerating three.

One `applyTitle()` reading `ctx.model` and `ctx.sessionManager` at call time, invoked from each registered handler, beats formatting the title per event — it mirrors how Pi itself funnels four call sites into `updateTerminalTitle()` (interactive-mode.js:810-819, called at :851, :1602, :1914, :2801).

Routing Pi's model through the terminal title is consistent with the mechanism already shipped rather than a new channel: the model mark is title-derived by design (source/CHANGELOG.md:15, source/README.md:95-98), and `MODEL_FALLBACK` (source/lib/logos.js:257) exists precisely for harnesses that do not say. Adding `pi` to that table would be the provider-hardcoding bullet 3 rules out, and would be unnecessary once the title carries the model.

Narrowing F3 would be cheap and local: matching against the model id alone rather than the whole title, or anchoring the model token in the title with a delimiter the family regexes cannot straddle, keeps bullet 4's promise without touching the family table. Non-blocking as a design preference, but F3 itself is not.
